_about: The parity gate's configuration (tests/parity/compare.mjs). `gates` names what the gate holds: `full` routes are compared whole (landmarks by role and name, headings, controls, list containers and rows, row heights at 375); `frame` routes only for the shell the slice draws (frameControls, frameHeadings); `pixelExact` routes also gate on the 2 percent pixel diff; `lists` routes must have rows in their baseline. Every name in routes.json is gated or listed in `exempt` with a reason (gateProblems, tested). A gated route that is not compared is a FAIL unless `skippable` names it with a reason; the report ends `compared N of M gated routes`. `listEmpty` names a list route whose baseline account legitimately holds no rows. `approved` lists the differences from the baseline that a ruling allows, each with its ruling; nothing else may differ. It is empty because the baseline is the new production site (2026-10-19); a waiver must match a current difference, and the report ends with the `unused waivers:` line. `rulings` is text only.

exempt.reason: no baseline exists: the console is the platform admin's account data and the baseline job holds no admin sign-in. The deployed-preview capture (PARITY_ADMIN=1) still records it and its offences fail the compare; the layout is held at four widths by admin-smoke over populated mocks.

skippable.reason: baseline owed: the member account holds no group, so the capture finds no group page to discover (tests/parity/baseline/README.md). Capture it once the account joins a group, then delete this entry.

listEmpty.reason: the baseline account follows nothing (dash-search-smoke compares the empty state), so its list holds no rows; the rows are compared the day the account follows an item.

dataNames.match: ^(Global|EU|United States|United Kingdom|Asia.Pacific|Latin America|Middle East & Africa) room
dataNames.keep: ^(Global|EU|United States|United Kingdom|Asia.Pacific|Latin America|Middle East & Africa) room
dataNames.reason: the seven room tiles are named by live data (the item count, then the three leading theme words drawn from the ledger); they compare by the room name
the archive list is account data (the item a team archived is named by the live ledger); Restore buttons compare by their stable prefix and the "for the whole team" scope is held by the fixture row

rulings: Text only, not matching waivers. Retired 2026-10-19 (P2-15p) when the baseline became the new production site: the differences against the old site no longer exist, so their waivers are gone; the look decisions stay recorded here.

ux-laws.md law 2 (binding, DP-2): every control is at least 44 px. Artboard 16 draws 36 px auth fields (DESIGN CHANGES OWED 1); the artboard-01 privacy nav card rows are 44 px (pitch 46) where the artboard draws about 42 (OWED 10); the nav cap draws no band split while counts are unknown (rule 2 / INV-263, OWED 11). Structure still gates.

facet-row-desktop (operator 2026-10-18, on Claude Design's recommendation, WCAG 2.5.8): law 2 exception for the desktop Filters card only; facet rows keep a 24 px target on a 32 px pitch (24 px with 8 px clear) on desktop and 44 px on the phone (DESIGN CHANGES OWED 2).

Retired with the same change: the single-main landmark (ASSEMBLY H.1, the shell supplies the one main), SEC-5 assignee names, tie-order and row-height waivers, and the settings, profile, market, research and map look waivers; each was a difference from the old site only.

approved.ruling: K:50 and rule 20 (operator 2026-10-20, the coordinator's ruling on the research-detail red of PR 70): a fact card's source link and tier are read from the claim its paragraph names (a claim marker, migration 0108_data_claim_markers), never inferred from text. The cards the old containment rule linked wrongly (ambiguous text, first match) lose their provenance link by design; only the card provenance links ('host ↗') are covered.
